details.description: Qwen2.5-Coder-3B-Instruct is the instruction-tuned, 3.09-billion-parameter (2.77B non-embedding) member of Alibaba's Qwen2.5-Coder family, built on Qwen2.5-3B and trained on 5.5 trillion tokens covering source code, text-code grounding, and synthetic data. Released by Qwen on November 12, 2024 as part of the family's expansion beyond the original 1.5B/7B sizes, it is tuned for direct use in code generation, reasoning, and debugging rather than requiring further fine-tuning. It carries a Qwen Research license rather than the Apache 2.0 license Qwen uses for most other Qwen2.5-Coder sizes.
advantages: Instruction-tuned for direct use in code generation, reasoning, and debugging, unlike the base 3B checkpoint it is built from, per Qwen's model card.
Trained on 5.5 trillion tokens including source code, text-code grounding, and synthetic data, per Qwen's model card.
Documented by Qwen as a comprehensive foundation for real-world code agent applications, per Qwen's model card.
Retains general math and reasoning competence alongside its coding focus, per Qwen's model card.
disadvantages: Text-only chat model with no vision or audio input, per Qwen's model card.
Released under a Qwen Research license, more restrictive for commercial use than the Apache 2.0 license Qwen uses for the larger Qwen2.5-Coder sizes.
use_cases: Code agent workflows, per Qwen's model card
General reasoning and mathematics tasks alongside coding

notes: No numeric benchmark scores for this specific 3B size are shown in text on Qwen's model card or the Qwen2.5-Coder blog (the blog only shows size-vs-score charts for smaller sizes, not tabulated numbers), so evaluations is left empty rather than guessed. Qwen's GitHub repo for Qwen2.5-Coder now redirects (HTTP 301) to QwenLM/Qwen3-Coder, so no working github_url could be confirmed; left null. Release date corrected to November 12, 2024 (the family's four-size expansion announcement): the HF repo's first commit is Nov 6, 2024. The model card's boilerplate only documents 'Code Agents' as a named use case; 'program synthesis', 'code review' and 'tool-calling' were not found on any current Qwen page and were removed/trimmed.
